- Suggested pricing and one‑time onboarding credit (see invoice appendix)

4) Procurement wants a DocuSign link and a PO for the new commit. Can you send both and confirm earliest practical cutover date if our PO clears Oct 28?

Subject: Re: Renewal: upgrade reserved pool 8→16 GPUs — details + ops playbook

Elliot — thanks for the clear list. Answers below and I attached the activation_playbook_v1.pdf so your infra/procurement can scan the steps.

1) Pricing: committed rate = $17,500 / GPU-month (net) for the 16‑GPU reservation; total = $280,000 / month. The proposal PDF breaks the line items and shows the one‑time onboarding credit we discussed.

2) Burst buffer: the 10% buffer is reserved capacity applied as short‑term headroom for prefix caching and transient spikes. It is managed by the routing layer and is guaranteed for short windows (up to 5 minutes per minute of spike); sustained use beyond the buffer will prompt autoscaling policies (charged at committed rate if within pooled reserved capacity, otherwise billed per-usage). We can scope a larger burst or a higher holdback if you anticipate long sustained windows.

3) SLA / throughput: we guarantee sustained throughput for the reserved pool expressed as aggregate tokens/sec at 95th percentile for sustained 30‑minute windows. For the 16‑GPU pool the baseline guarantee is 620K tokens/min aggregated (see SLA appendix). Latency percentiles are also maintained — we include 95th and 99th tail metrics in the console.

4) DocuSign + PO: DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/doc/ABC123 (live proposal). Once you confirm the PO date I’ll ask finance to align proration. If your PO clears Oct 28 we recommend targeted activation on Nov 3 to align with your month‑start and give us two business days to run the canary.

Activation playbook highlights (attached):
- Canary lane (2 GPUs) for 48 hours with synthetic traffic and sampling of real traffic
- Partial roll (50% of traffic) for 72 hours with SLA monitoring and automated rollback triggers for QoS regressions
- Full cutover and 14‑day safety holdback window where Redis/Prefix cache warmups are prioritized
- Rollback window: automated rollback can be triggered in <4 hours if latency > 2x baseline or error rates exceed 0.5% for any 15‑minute window

CCing Laura (Finance) and Marissa (CS Ops) to confirm pricing netting, PO acceptance, and any onboarding credit approvals.

Attachments: activation_playbook_v1.pdf 

Regards,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
